focus: σαν + bare noun = 'like a sister' vs όπως for real comparisons – say it in plain words, drop the Greek-language jargon 'αιτιατική', romanize όπως.
μου αρέσει works backwards – the liked person is the grammatical subject ('he pleases me'), which is why the verb isn't first person.
εδώ και + time span with the present tense = English 'have been ... for' – keep the ongoing-span insight, romanize the full example εδώ και δύο χρόνια.
παντρεύομαι looks passive but means plain active 'marry' – introduce the -ομαι verb family in plain words (these verbs only exist in this form), no 'deponent' jargon.
the object pronoun comes before the verb – μας σύστησαν is 'us they-introduced'; teach the pronoun-first order, cut the aorist trivia and the 'clitic' jargon.
μεταξύ τους (literally 'between them') is how Greek says 'each other' – keep the reciprocity point, add romanization for μεταξύ τους.
μοιάζω σε ('resemble TO someone') = take after – the σε instead of a direct object is the trap; romanize the cited chunks.
αντέχω vs μπορώ – 'can't bear/stand' vs plain 'can't'; keep the strength contrast, romanize δεν μπορώ too.
δεμένη is literally 'tied' – Greek families are tied where English ones are knit; romanize the full phrase δεμένη οικογένεια.
the dummy τα – τα πάω καλά carries an unexplained 'them', a fixed-idiom pattern (same family as τα βρίσκω); romanize every Greek chunk.
τα βρίσκω 'find them' = make up – second telling of the dummy-τα idiom family; anchor to ας τα βρούμε and romanize fully.
sole survivor of its 3-member dup group – the -θηκα past of feeling verbs looks passive: φοβήθηκα 'I got scared'; generalize the pattern (λυπήθηκα, θυμήθηκα) instead of restating the paradigm.
English says 'interested IN' but Greek uses για ('for') – keep the preposition mismatch, romanize για.
imperfect for repeated past – χαιρόμουν pairs with κάθε φορά ('every time'); the ongoing/repeated-past aspect is the insight, not the paradigm of χαίρομαι.
the verb agrees with the thing liked – το ρεμπέτικο is one thing so μου αρέσει stays singular; romanize το ρεμπέτικο.
plural things liked flip the verb – τα τραγούδια → μου αρέσουν; romanize τα τραγούδια.
ανεβάζω 'raise' = upload/release in the online sense – keep the raise-to-upload landmine; romanize τραγούδι.
θερινό σινεμά, the open-air summer cinema ritual – keep the cultural hook; romanize σινεμά too.
κόσμος means 'world' AND 'people/crowd' – γεμάτος κόσμο is literally 'full of world'; state both meanings instead of hinting with 'here'.
παρακολουθώ vs βλέπω – the formal watch/follow verb for shows and documentaries; keep the register contrast, romanize βλέπω.
prefer X to Y takes από ('from'), not παρά – keep the contrast, romanize από and παρά.
a TV season is a κύκλος 'cycle' in Greek – English 'season' vs Greek 'cycle'; romanize σειράς.
Epidaurus's ancient theater still hosts summer plays – keep the cultural fact; romanize θέατρο.
imperfect έπαιζαν paints the ongoing performance ('they were performing') – teach the aspect angle in plain words, not 'imperfect of παίζω' trivia.
σειρά = row AND series – front row vs a TV σειρά; romanize πρώτη σειρά.
ανεβάζω 'raise' = stage/put on a play – pairs with the upload sense as a second telling; romanize παράσταση.
σκηνικό (the set) vs σκηνή (the stage) – keep the pair, romanize σκηνή.
πίνακας = painting AND (black)board – keep the landmine, cut the 'accusative singular' jargon tail.
photos are 'taken out' in Greek: βγάζω φωτογραφία, never παίρνω – keep the wrong-verb trap, romanize παίρνω.
Greek has no plain 'borrow' verb – παίρνω δανεικό 'take (it) lent'; keep the structure, romanize παίρνω too.
δυνατά = 'loudly/aloud' AND 'strongly' – reading aloud anchors the landmine; romanize διαβάζω.
δοκίμιο (literary essay) vs έκθεση (school essay) – keep the pair, romanize έκθεση.
κινώ το ενδιαφέρον is literally 'move the interest' – keep the literal hook, romanize the full phrase.
πριν takes the να-style verb form (Greek has no infinitive) – πριν κοιμηθώ 'before I sleep'; say it without 'perfective' jargon.
